subject: Mathematics
title: Why 0.999… Equals 1
summary: 0.999… with the 9s never stopping is exactly 1, not "a little less". Three short proofs show why.
keyPoints: 0.999 with three 9s is less than 1; only the **never-ending** 0.999… equals 1.

blocks.alt: Bars showing the gap to 1 shrinking with more 9s
blocks.caption: Each extra 9 shrinks the gap; with endless 9s no gap is left.

blocks.p: Between any two different numbers there is always another (their average). Try to find one between 0.999… and 1: there is none, so they are the same number.

list: The same trick works for any recurring decimal: 0.777… = 7/9, 0.4545… = 45/99 = 5/11.
Every terminating decimal has a recurring-9 twin: 0.5 = 0.4999…
Recurring decimals are rational numbers (they can be written as p/q).

quiz.explain: It is exactly 1: 0.999… and 1 are two names for the same number.
With a finite number of 9s there is a gap (here 0.001). Only the never-ending 0.999… equals 1.

simulation.reason: A proof-based idea: the three proofs and the shrinking-gap picture carry it; an interactive slider would only repeat the picture.
